row.name: My Little Rascals New Start Cdc

occurrences.finding: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary: During an inspection of the daycare kitchen, it was observed that food items were present in the handwashing sink.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary (26 TAC §746.3317)

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: A crib mattress was observed in a damaged condition, with exposed internal padding and a visible metal support component. The mattress did not provide a safe, intact sleep surface for children. This was corrected at inspection, and the mattress was exchanged for another.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Diaper Changing Steps-Supplies Kept Out of Child's Reach: During the inspection, diaper cream was observed inside a child storage area. It was noted that the diaper cream was accessible to toddlers in the classroom. This was corrected during the inspection, and the item was removed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diaper Changing Steps-Supplies Kept Out of Child's Reach (26 TAC §746.3501(6))

occurrences.finding: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner: In the toddler classroom, there were two trash cans containing garbage that was easily accessible to the children. This was corrected during the inspection the trash was removed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3407(8))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups: Two bottles in the infant room were not labeled during the inspection. This was corrected at inspection Staff labeled bottles.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups (26 TAC §746.2419(6))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: During the inspection, a television cord was observed hanging down the wall within reach of children in the one-year-old classroom. The exposed cord posed a potential strangulation and electrical hazard to children in care. The operation did not ensure that the area was free from hazards accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Rotating and Rocking Equipment (Sitting): During the inspection, I observed a spring-mounted school bus" climber located less than six feet from the chain-link fence. This was corrected at inspection. The outdoor equipment was moved to meet use zone requirements.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Rotating and Rocking Equipment (Sitting) (26 TAC §746.4813(a))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: The infant classroom door is missing screws, making it difficult to open and creating a safety hazard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: The operation did not have a list of children being transported to and from school.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age: During the inspection, it was observed that a child was sleeping in a chair instead of on a mat or cot.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age (26 TAC §746.4503(a))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing Before Eating: Children were observed being fed before washing their hands. This was corrected during the inspection afte addressing the concerns with staff.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing Before Eating (26 TAC §746.3417(1))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: Caregivers who were supervising children alone did not have their current certification.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption with HS Diploma/GED- Not in Charge of Group: A caregiver who was not of legal age was responsible for supervising a group of children alone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Caregiver Qualification Age Exemption with HS Diploma/GED- Not in Charge of Group (26 TAC §746.1109(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: During the investigation, it was determined that the permit holder and director were made aware of a situation that placed children at risk and failed to notify child care regulation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Caregiver Skills/Needs of Children: On 6/26/25 during the inspection it was detemened that Staff did not demonstrate the necessary skills to manage the assigned group, and there was no documented training or evaluation of the caregiver's qualifications at the time of inspection.      During a Child Care Investigation (CCI), it was determined that the caregiver responsible for eight 12- to 18-month-old children lacked the necessary training and skills to adequately care for this number of children and manage an additional child who was a known runner.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Caregiver Skills/Needs of Children (26 TAC §746.1507(3))

occurrences.finding: Meal preparation, except when 12 or fewer children are in care: A caregiver responsible for supervising a group of children was preparing lunch for the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Meal preparation, except when 12 or fewer children are in care (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(B))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director did not ensure there was enough staff present to manage day-to-day responsibilities in the director's absence. The director left a caregiver in charge of the operation who was also responsible for supervising a group of children and preparing meals.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Staff did not provide adequate care, considering the known needs of a child with a history of running. Failing to account for this behavior put the child at risk. The child got out of the building and was unaccounted for, for 18 minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Caregiver Skills/Needs of Children: During a Child Care Investigation (CCI), it was determined that the caregiver responsible for eight 12- to 18-month-old children lacked the necessary training and skills to adequately care for this number of children and manage an additional child who was a known runner.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Caregiver Skills/Needs of Children (26 TAC §746.1507(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers: During a CCI investigation, interviews with staff revealed that a caregiver failed to inform the incoming caregiver that a child was back in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers (26 TAC §746.1203(10))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During a CCI investigation, it was determined that caregivers did not provide adequate supervision. A child exited the operation and was found by a bystander leaving the child unaccounted for 18 minutes.    A total of four children were seen on video unsupervised in two different hallways. Two caregivers were seen on the video and did not intervene to ensure appropriate supervision of the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Children were seen walking the hallway without a caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The facility school age building contains visible holes in the walls, a sinking floor, bulging carpet, a cracked ceiling, and a nonfunctional toilet. Additionally, a strong odor is present throughout the building.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: The center fire inspection has expired as of 12/20/24
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: An infant was observed sleeping in a crib with a Pacifier Clip Holder connected to their clothing. This was corrected at inspection, the clip was removed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets: An infant was observed sleeping in a crib with a loose mattress sheet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Installation of Unitary Surfacing Materials - to Manufacturer's Specifications: The turf on the playground has not been maintained per the manufacturer's requirements. This poses a tripping hazard.The turf has been reomved.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation of Unitary Surfacing Materials - to Manufacturer's Specifications (26 TAC §746.4911(a))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups: Infant bottles were not labeled as required. This was corrected during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Label Bottles/Cups (26 TAC §746.2419(6))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: The center has not conducted a fire drill for the months of February and April
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: Complying with Laws and Rules: The permit holder failed to meet several regulatory responsibilities. Issues included failure to report to CCR, inadequate supervision, and poor building conditions. Annual health and fire inspections were not up to date, and safe sleep practices were not followed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Complying with Laws and Rules (26 TAC §746.201(9))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The current health inspection has expired as of 4/3/2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The director failed to ensure that the childcare operation was fully compliant with Child Care Regulation (CCR) requirements, resulting in multiple areas of noncompliance.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Infant Not in Crib with Drop Gate Down: Infants were observed inside cribs with the drop gate open. This was corrected during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Infant Not in Crib with Drop Gate Down (26 TAC §746.2409(c))

occurrences.finding: Smoke Detectors Testing: The smoke detector in the school building is beeping.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Smoke Detectors Testing (26 TAC §746.5319)

occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities: Video surveillance footage reviewed showed that children were watching television shows unrelated to the planned activity. Young children were watching Mickey Mouse Club, while older children were viewing YouTube.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Related to Planned Activities (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment when they placed a three-year-old child in a highchair meant for 9?to 24-month-olds for over 15 minutes to prevent the child from leaving the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: A caregiver was observed on video using her cell phone while the children were watching television.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Video surveillance footage provided by center showed children under two years old watching the Mickey Mouse Club on television.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two (26 TAC §746.2207(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver leaving the classroom failed to communicate to the incoming caregiver that they were no longer responsible for supervising the classroom. occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Service and Preparation Requirement - Safe and Sanitary (26 TAC §746.3317)

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: Several classrooms observed had broken light fixtures, soiled damaged ceiling tiles and walls.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: A classroom observed had exposed risk. The vinyl wall base trim had come off  exposing chipped paint and glue.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Electrical Outlets Covered: Several classrooms were found to lack safety outlet covers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Electrical Outlets Covered (26 TAC §746.3701(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: This standard was assigned as part of an investigation and was found to be deficient. A review of video surveillance footage reveals a caregiver striking two children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The center did not notify CCR within the required timeframe.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A caregiver demonstrated a lack of good judgment when they did not make an attempt to separate children involved in a physical altercation. Additionally, a caregiver did not follow the operation's policy regarding pick up procedures. The caregiver did not ask to see identification or ask for a code word of an authorized pick-up person that was picking up for the first time.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children: During an inspection, it was observed that one caregiver was outside with 40 children aged 17 months to 12 years old. This was corrected during the inspection, and the children were taken to separate classrooms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1601)

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A volunteer with a pending background check  had direct access to children in care. The volunteer left and fingerprint was schedule.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver was seen using their personal cell phone while three infants played near an open refrigerator.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))
